Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

knbsdata (development version)

Health and demography from the KDHS

KNBS implements the Kenya Demographic and Health Surveys, and the DHS Program publishes their indicators through its Indicator Data API, now a source ("dhs_program"): 4,115 indicators from the KDHS of 1989 to 2022 and the 2015 and 2020 Malaria Indicator Surveys, through the same knbs_indicators() and knbs_get_indicator() as every other source.

  • Each indicator comes for every survey that measured it, by background characteristic (residence, wealth, education and others), by the former provinces, and from 2014 for the 47 counties, with 2019 census county codes so they join the census tables: knbs_get_indicator("CN_NUTS_C_HA2", geo_level = "county").
  • Where the DHS Program gives values for several reference periods, all are kept and preferred marks its choice. An id the API reuses for two indicators, serving two values for one survey and group, is refused rather than guessed at (audit F-42).
  • knbs_cite() gives the citation the API’s terms ask for, and no longer repeats a URL that a source’s own citation already names.
  • knbs_search() finds them. Search now reads -ing and -ed as endings, so “stunting” matches “Children stunted”, and “KDHS” finds the survey’s indicators. Scoring is vectorised, stemming each distinct word once, so ranking the 6,000-odd rows it now searches takes about a second rather than eight.
  • knbs_county_code() falls back on the 47 counties’ statutory codes, the census frame’s own and held identical by the tests, when the census service cannot be reached.
  • The API’s robots file bars its own /rest/dhs/ path to every client, while its documentation invites applications to use it. The package reads the rule as one for crawlers: it requests only what is asked for, one indicator at a time, under its own name, throttled and cached. The README’s access conditions now say how robots rules are read, and the audit records the reasoning.
  • The test suite now fails any test that would reach the network.

Open survey microdata: FinAccess

The FinAccess household survey, Kenya’s survey of financial inclusion by the Central Bank of Kenya, KNBS and FSD Kenya, publishes its anonymised, weighted microdata for anyone to download. The package now reaches it.

  • knbs_finaccess_files() lists 22 files: the microdata of six household rounds (2006, 2009, 2013, 2016, 2021 and 2024) and two waves of the MSE Tracker Survey (2022 and 2023), in Stata, SPSS or Excel, with the questionnaires, manuals and reports. The catalogue ships with the package and records what each portal link actually serves: four of the portal’s labels are wrong, and its 2006 and 2009 “Questionnaire” archives hold the data (audit F-40).
  • knbs_download_finaccess() downloads them under their official names. A sixteen-byte request checks each file’s served name and size before it moves; its size and SHA-256 are checked after, against checksums taken from full downloads of every file. A file already downloaded and identical is reused without a request, so knbs_read_microdata(knbs_download_finaccess("hh2024-stata")) is safe to re-run. The 2013 survey’s Stata copy, behind a registration form on Harvard Dataverse, is listed and never fetched.
  • knbs_read_microdata() reads Stata, SPSS and Excel files and the data inside a .zip, keeping value and variable labels, and attaches the provenance in the file’s sidecar, so knbs_cite() cites the producers. It also reads files obtained through the national archive’s own process.
  • knbs_search() has a "microdata" type: one result per survey round, whose get call downloads and reads it.
  • Downloads stream to disk instead of through memory, and are abandoned only once stalled for the timeout’s length rather than when the timeout runs out, so a 300 MB file on a slow line completes.
  • knbs_status(live = TRUE) checks that the portal still links every catalogued file.

The portal states no licence. FSD Kenya’s terms for the 2013 survey restrict it to research and forbid redistribution without written agreement, so assume nothing wider: the terms travel in each file’s sidecar and metadata, the first download of a session names the producers, and no file is bundled with the package.

One provenance record per file

Provenance sidecars are now named after the whole file name: pop.dta gets pop.dta.metadata.json, where it used to get pop.metadata.json. The old name was shared by every file with the same stem, so knbs_write()-ing a table as pop.csv and pop.dta into one folder, or downloading a survey’s Stata and SPSS copies side by side, left only the last file’s record. Sidecars written by earlier versions keep their old names.

Quieter lookups

knbs_get_indicator() resolves an indicator against every source’s catalogue, and warned “Could not reach: …” on every call while any one portal was down — even for an indicator served by another source. It now stays silent when the id is found in a source that answered. A name search still warns, since the unreachable catalogue might hold another match, and a not-found error names the unreachable source as a possible reason. The README leads its live examples with the most dependable sources and says what an outage looks like.

Twelve more Statistical Abstract chapters

knbs_abstract_table() now serves 48 tables of the 2025 Statistical Abstract, up from Chapter 2’s fifteen: 33 more from Chapters 3–16 — wage employment by sector; the Post Office Savings Bank and insurance business; principal export commodities; crop sales and producer prices; forest plantations and wildlife; electricity connections and fuel sales; producer price indices and production of selected commodities; construction output by county and cement; visitor arrivals, departures and hotel occupancy; railway earnings, vehicle registration and inspection, Mombasa port and aircraft; school enrolment, by county too; and registered births and deaths by county. Each has a curated recipe, totals checked against their parts where the table has them, and pinned figures (audit F-39).

  • County tables carry census codes. Six tables are by county; their rows get geo_code, the census frame code, through the county matching of knbs_county_code() (the total row is "00"), so registered births join the census population in one step. A county table is refused if its rows stop accounting for the 47 counties exactly once.
  • Per-row units come through as a unit column where a sheet prints them (sugar in tonnes, soft drinks in thousands of litres).
  • Footnotes keep their meaning. Marks printed against labels (“Coffee1,2”) are removed, and what they said — auction prices, revised years, what a category includes — is in knbs_metadata()’s notes, with the source each sheet credits.
  • A layout trap is now refused. Table 3.11 puts Male | Female | Total under each year; the engine skipped that unlabelled second header row and would have read each year’s Male column as the year’s value. Any such row now stops extraction with knbs_error_schema_changed.

A survey of all 267 tables in the chapter workbooks found 38 in the layout the engine reads; the 33 curated are those, less four tables split across two sheets and Table 3.11.

What KNBS has released lately

New knbs_releases() lists what KNBS has put on its website, newest first: the last 30 days by default, any window with since and until, or one series’ whole history with series = "cpi". Each row carries its release series, the period it covers and the call that downloads it.

  • Series are KNBS’s regular releases, read from titles by a curated list (knbs_release_series()): the monthly CPI and inflation release and Leading Economic Indicators; quarterly GDP, balance of payments and trade, producer, construction-input and residential property price indices, and labour force reports; the Economic Survey, Facts and Figures, national and county Statistical Abstracts, Gross County Product and the Advance Release Calendar. Patterns allow for the library’s own spellings (“Proprety”, “Leading Economic Indicators- March 2026”).
  • period is the month ("2026-09") or quarter ("2026-Q2") a title names, NA otherwise. It matters because the date is the upload date: years of older releases were uploaded together when the library was set up in mid-2023.
  • Tenders, adverts, vacancies and other notices — 23 of 2026’s first 151 uploads — are left out unless notices = TRUE.

Live: the last 30 days give the September 2026 CPI release and July’s Leading Economic Indicators; the CPI series holds 255 distinct months.

Fixes

  • Citations dated a retrieval in UTC, so anything retrieved between midnight and 03:00 in Nairobi was cited as retrieved the day before. The plain, BibTeX and RIS citations now use the local date.

Files for Excel, Stata and SPSS, provenance included

New knbs_write() saves a result for colleagues who do not use R, and the provenance goes with it. The format follows the extension:

  • .xlsx — a data sheet and an about sheet: title, producer, source and URL, release date, reference period, unit, licence, retrieval time, package version, the source’s notes, and a ready-made citation.
  • .csv, .dta (Stata, the title as dataset label) and .sav (SPSS) — with a <file>.metadata.json sidecar, the one publication downloads already write.
  • .rds — the object whole, metadata inside.

Codes stay text in every format ("01", never 1). Stata’s 32-character limit shortens longer names, keeping their _code or _type ending and uniqueness, with the full name as the variable label and every rename recorded. List columns are written as JSON text and named in the provenance. A table derived with summarise() or a pivot is plain data: pass metadata = knbs_metadata(original) and its file carries the source’s provenance; without it the file is written with a warning and says no provenance was attached. An existing file is never replaced unless overwrite = TRUE. writexl and haven join Suggests.

County names, matched across sources

County names are not spelled alike even inside KNBS: the census writes “Murang’a”, “Tharaka-Nithi” and “Nairobi City”, the Data Portal “MURANGA”, “THARAKA NITHI” and “NAIROBI”, each under its own codes. New knbs_county_code() turns county names — or numbers — written any way into the census frame’s two-digit codes, ready for mutate() and a join; new knbs_match_counties() shows how each value matched.

  • A name matches once case, punctuation, spacing and apostrophes are set aside and “County”, “City”, “Government”, “of” and “the” are dropped: “Taita/Taveta”, “Taita Taveta” and “TAITA-TAVETA COUNTY” are all "06". Numbers 1–47 are county numbers; “Kenya” and “National” are "00".
  • Nothing else is matched — no list of alternative names exists to guess from. A misspelling becomes NA with one knbs_warning_unmatched warning naming it and, where one official name is close, suggesting it (“Kakamenga” → did you mean “Kakamega”?).
  • Verified live: all 48 names the Data Portal’s county tables use match, to 48 distinct codes, and its rural-population table joins the census on all 47 counties. The county-data vignette works the example through.

One search across everything

New knbs_search() answers “where does this live?” in one call. It searches the indicator catalogues of every verified source, the survey archive, the publications library and the curated Abstract tables, and returns one ranked table — each row with get, the exact call that retrieves it: knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", source = "knbs_cpi"), knbs_abstract_table("2.2"), knbs_survey_metadata(...), knbs_download_publication(...).

  • Matching is the package’s own, over each catalogue in full, so it means the same everywhere: every word must appear in a title, id or topic. Words match by stem — the library’s own search is literal, and for “consumer price index” returns 2 documents while KNBS publishes a “Consumer Price Indices and Inflation Rates” release every month; this finds them all — and four-letter prefixes match longer words. CPI, GDP, GCP, GVA, PPI, BOP, KDHS, KIHBS and LEI are understood both ways.
  • Ranking is by tier — exact id, exact title, the query as a phrase, every word in the title, a match elsewhere — then data before documents and newer before older, so the CPI series leads a CPI search and the latest monthly release follows it.
  • Catalogues are cached for a day. The first search of the day lists the whole publications library (about 16 requests); later ones take a second or two. An unreachable catalogue is a warning naming it; the error comes only when nothing answers.

Rough edges: a silent row loss, readable columns, totals and parts

A live review on 2026-10-05 turned up places where correct data was still easy to misuse, or where it was not correct at all.

  • A Statistical Abstract row was being dropped silently. The “Tree, crop and plant resources yielding repeat products” row of Tables 2.7a and 2.7c reads 7866, 8269, 8922, … — four-digit cells the extractor took for a repeated year header and skipped, so capital formation’s parts no longer added up to its Total. A header is now recognised only as a run of consecutive years, and a repeat only as the same years in the same columns. The row is pinned in the registry so it cannot drop out again.

  • Totals and their parts are told apart. The Abstract prints “GDP at market prices”, “All industries”, each industry and its sub-industries in one column, so summing a year counted GDP several times over. Tables 2.2–2.7d now carry parent, the row each item is a component of (NA for headline totals and memo items): filter(parent == "All industries") gives the industries and nothing else. The structure is curated in the extraction registry and verified on every read — every named row must be present, and in the level and share tables the parts must add up to their parent in every year within what rounding explains. Had this existed, it would have caught the dropped row above. Imports enter GDP with a negative sign, and knbs_metadata() says so. The accounts tables (2.1, 2.8, 2.9) are linked by identities, not parts and totals, and carry none.

  • Readable dimension columns — a breaking change. Indicator dimensions were <id>/<id>_label pairs named by the source’s internal ids (p18_vs1, NA_INDIC). Every source now follows the geo_name/ geo_code pattern: <name> holds the labels and <name>_code the codes. Census tables use curated names — marital_status, age, religion, household_head_sex and the rest of the 29 dimensions the 2019 tables carry — because the API’s own labels are long and sometimes misspelt. Data Portal flows use their SDMX id in lower case (na_indic), since the portal labels ten different dimensions just “Indicator”. A Sex dimension is sex, lower-cased, everywhere. Code that read p18_vs1 == "T" now reads marital_status == "Total" (or marital_status_code == "T"); table == "T3" on Gross County Product becomes table_code == "T3".

  • Census ages that add up. The age table mixes single years with five-year groups and a total. New age_type ("total", "single_year", "age_group", "other") lets a pyramid keep one level; the groups are checked on every read to add up to the total and the single years to their group, which held exactly across all 393 areas when verified.

  • The Data Portal stopped declaring its geography (audit F-37). By October the hub sent an empty geo role where it named REF_AREA in August, so geo_code vanished and geography filters were refused. The SDMX reference-area concept now stands in when the role is empty, as TIME_PERIOD already did for time.

  • A CPI Explorer outage points somewhere useful (audit F-38). The Explorer’s data service answered HTTP 500 on 2026-10-05. Its errors now name the Data Portal series that stands in, and how closely: the portal’s DF_CPI_R index matched the Explorer to two decimals, but its inflation rates (DF_CPI_YR, DF_CPI_MR) are KNBS’s published, rounded figures and differed — May 2026 year on year was 6.9 there against 6.68 here. Nothing is substituted silently.

The cache moves to parser version 3 and schema version 2 (with the two source quirks below), so results cached in an older shape are re-fetched rather than served.

Two source quirks kept out of results

Both found by live testing on 2026-10-05.

  • Survey years of 0. KeNADA stores year_start and year_end as "0" for the 53 of its 131 studies catalogued without a reference year, and its year filter returns all of them for any year: knbs_search_surveys(year = 2022) came back with 54 rows, 53 of them dated "0" — the 2013 FinAccess National Survey among them. A year of 0 now standardises to NA, in reference_years and in knbs_survey_metadata()’s reference_period. A year filter is applied again client-side, matching a study whose years overlap the range; a study with no recorded year cannot match, so it is excluded, and a knbs_warning_missing_metadata warning says how many and names them in its excluded field. Years are never inferred from titles or ids. When the source matches more studies than one page holds, every match is fetched before filtering, so limit cannot shorten the count.
  • Census table titles. The census API labels every table “Census 2019 - Population by sex and marital status” (POPCEN0002, POPCEN0003 and POPCEN0004 all carry it), whatever the table holds. indicator_name and the metadata title now come from the dataset list — POPCEN0002 is “Population by Single and Grouped Ages, Sex and sub County” — and the source’s own label is recorded in knbs_metadata()$notes. Where the dataset list gives no name, the label stands and the notes say so.

The tidyverse contract, locked in tests

Every data-carrying result has always been a vctrs-backed tidy tibble; the behaviour is now guaranteed rather than incidental. Tests pin that dplyr verbs — filter(), mutate(), arrange(), select(), slice_max(), joins, bind_rows() — keep both the class and the provenance metadata (knbs_metadata() still answers on the result); that group_by() + summarise() and the tidyr pivots return plain tibbles, since a derived table is the caller’s data rather than the source’s; and that tibble::as_tibble() strips the wrapper cleanly. dplyr and tidyr join Suggests for these tests, and the getting-started and statistical-abstract vignettes now show the piped workflows, including pivot_wider() recreating the printed-table look.

The Statistical Abstract as tidy tables

The 2025 Statistical Abstract ships its chapter tables as Excel workbooks on the KNBS website (audit F-35). New knbs_abstract_tables() and knbs_abstract_table() turn the curated ones into clean tidy observations — starting with all fifteen tables of Chapter 2, National Accounts: the production accounts, GDP by activity at current and constant prices, expenditure on GDP, capital formation, national income and saving.

  • Extraction is curated, never guessed (audit F-36). Each table has a hand-verified recipe — sheet, title anchor, section labels, unit, pinned reference values — and every read re-verifies all of it. A workbook whose layout or figures have drifted is refused with a classed error; plausible-but-wrong tidy data is the one outcome the design rules out.
  • The tidy shape keeps the table’s meaning: period (integer year), status carrying the source’s own provisional (*) and revised (+) year flags, the row dimension as a named column (industry, expenditure_category, purpose), sections as a second named column where the sheet has them, and rows the source prints without figures (“Less: Subsidies”) kept with honest NA values.
  • The workbook is fetched once through the existing verify-and-checksum layer, cached, and hashed; knbs_metadata() names the edition, sheet and workbook SHA-256 on every result, and knbs_cite() cites it.
  • The extraction registry (inst/extdata/abstract-registry.yml) is the extension point: further chapters and the legacy annex sheets can be curated without touching the engine. Requires the new readxl dependency.

Gross County Product, via the Open Data for Africa republisher

The county economy arrives as data — from the one portal that serves it. knbs_indicators() and knbs_get_indicator() now also serve kenya.opendataforafrica.org (opendataforafrica in the registry), the Knoema-operated portal listed on KNBS’s own portals page, which republishes 202 Kenyan datasets: 169 from KNBS under a “Public Domain” licence label, the rest from the Central Bank of Kenya, ministries and agencies (audit F-30). Chief among them: Gross County Product (knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc")) — GVA shares plus constant- and current-price GCP for all 47 counties, annual 2013–2020, which no first-party KNBS portal serves as data.

  • This is a republisher, and the package says so: every result’s knbs_metadata() names the portal, the original producer, the dataset’s own licence label (verbatim; “Not stated by the source” where there is none) and the portal’s publication and update dates — so a vintage that lags the producer’s newest PDFs is visible, never hidden. The GCP dataset is the 2021 edition; newer GCP years remain PDF-only.
  • New frequency argument to knbs_get_indicator(). A portal dataset may mix annual, quarterly and monthly series under one id (audit F-33); annual periods are integer years and sub-annual ones are Dates, which cannot share a column, so a mixed dataset asks you to choose (frequency = "annual") instead of picking one silently. Sources where the filter means nothing refuse it.
  • Every series’ timeline is expanded from its own start date and verified against its own stated end date; a mismatch is refused as a schema change rather than shifting values onto wrong years. Geography codes are the portal’s own region codes (geo_level NA) and must never be joined against knbs_geographies(); the listing’s structural fields are not trusted (audit F-32), and the portal’s 200-with-a-string error answers are classed as missing resources (audit F-31).
  • Unstated start/end bounds no longer imply a default window: previously observations before 2000 (and, for sub-annual series, after the current month) were silently trimmed even when no bounds were asked for. No verified source served such observations until now, so no earlier result changes; the bounds you do state behave exactly as before.

The KNBS Data Portal: 323 dataflows

The economy arrives as data. knbs_indicators() and knbs_get_indicator() now also serve the KNBS Data Portal (knbs_opendata in the registry) — an SDMX hub carrying 323 dataflows across five statistical domains: GDP by activity and by expenditure, GFCF, GNI, production accounts, CPI by division and by region, balance of payments, trade, money and banking, county government finance, employment, agriculture, tourism, health and justice (audit F-28).

  • Dataflow ids are the SDMX ids, e.g. knbs_get_indicator("DF_NAT_GDPCP") for GDP by activity at current prices. Annual flows carry integer-year periods; monthly and quarterly flows carry first-of-period Dates — the same conventions as everywhere else, and start/end work unchanged.
  • The payload’s own role field names the time and geography dimensions, so neither is guessed. Hub geography codes are SDMX area codes, not census territories, and geo_level is NA rather than invented; do not join them against knbs_geographies().
  • Dimensions with a single category are facts about the whole dataflow — “Prices = Current prices”, “Unit = Kenya Shillings” — and fold into knbs_metadata() notes instead of arriving as constant columns.
  • Data queries are POSTs with a JSON criteria body (a GET answers 405); the responses are JSON-stat with sparse values, parsed by the same generic parser the census adapter uses. The portal states no licence, and the metadata say so.

knbsdata 0.4.0

Retail prices join the CPI family: what a kilogram of maize flour, a litre of petrol or a month’s single-room rent actually costs, monthly back to 2019.

  • New knbs_retail_prices(): the monthly national average retail prices of the 22 commodities tracked for the CPI basket — maize flour, milk, petrol, house rent and the rest — in Kenya Shillings per stated unit, with the full history the CPI Explorer holds (audit F-27). Filter by commodity code or name and by period; a single month is fetched directly, a range walks the paginated listing once and caches it. National only: the source holds no regional retail prices, so no region argument exists. The portal’s unstated licence is carried in the result’s metadata, as for the CPI series.

knbsdata 0.3.0

Consumer prices arrive as data, completing the plan’s headline example: knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", start = "2020-01").

Consumer prices

  • Three new indicators from the KNBS CPI Explorer (knbs_cpi in the registry): CPI_ALL_ITEMS (index points), CPI_INFLATION_YOY and CPI_INFLATION_MOM (percent) — monthly from January 2009, nationally and by the CPI collection strata (the Nairobi income bands, Nairobi Combined, Rest of Urban). Monthly observations carry period as a first-of-month Date plus a period_label; start and end accept a year, a month or a date, and now also bound census tables by their year.
  • knbs_indicators() aggregates every verified indicator source, with a source_id column; one unreachable source degrades the catalogue with a warning, and a single requested source that fails keeps its own error class instead of a generic “unreachable”.
  • Honesty, carried in knbs_metadata() on every CPI result: the portal states no licence and no index base period, and its regions are collection strata that must never be joined against knbs_geographies(). Six listed regions — the former provinces — carry no data in any period (audit F-26); asking for them returns zero rows because that is the source’s answer.
  • Defences from the audit: a requested region is validated against the source’s own region list before any data request, and a returned series that was not asked for is refused — the endpoint otherwise substitutes the national series for unknown regions silently (F-24). Date bounds are enforced client-side even though the server honoured them when traced.

Other

  • knbs_publications() with a format filter now pages back through older uploads until it has limit matches, instead of filtering only the most recent page. The live server ignores its file-type parameter (audit F-22), so a run of recent PDFs used to hide every workbook behind them — knbs_publications(format = "xlsx") could return nothing while dozens of Excel files existed. A record repeated across a page boundary by a mid-scan upload is kept once, running one page past the end is treated as the end, and a 5,000-document scan cap warns rather than trailing off silently.

knbsdata 0.2.0

Three new source families join the survey catalogue: publications, census tables as tidy indicators, and geographic reference codes. Every family is audited, adapter-built, tested offline against fixtures and verified live; vignette("source-status") states what each supports and what remains absent.

Geographic reference codes (Phase 6)

  • knbs_geographies() returns the 2019 census frame: Kenya, its 47 counties and their sub-counties, with names, structural parent codes and an explicit vintage column. Codes are character with leading zeros intact, read live from the census service’s own Territory dimension (CC BY 4.0) rather than shipped as a snapshot that could drift from the source.
  • A sub-county referencing a county the source did not list, or duplicate codes, are refused as validation failures rather than passed into joins.
  • Asking for any vintage other than 2019 fails with a clear error: no other vintage, no crosswalk and no boundary file has a verified source, and a wrong crosswalk is worse than none. Classifications remain unimplemented for the same reason. New vignette, county-data.

Census indicators (Phase 5)

The Phase 5 audit found a first-party machine-readable source: the KNBS census data service behind data.knbs.or.ke, built with Istat and serving 2019 Population and Housing Census tables as JSON-stat 2.0 under an explicit CC BY 4.0 statement.

  • knbs_indicators() lists the 32 tables across their themes (Population, Health, ICT, Household Farming).
  • knbs_get_indicator() returns a table as tidy observations: geography down to sub-county with leading zeros intact and a documented geo_level, sex in the source’s own categories, and every other dimension as a <dim_id>/<dim_id>_label column pair. Provenance carries the licence and the release date; citations work as everywhere else.
  • A generic JSON-stat 2.0 parser (dense and sparse values, status arrays, shape validation) with no KNBS specifics, ready for any future JSON-stat source.
  • The registry gains an explicit http_only flag: the census API host has no TLS listener, and the exception is declared and validated rather than slipped past the HTTPS rule. Traffic to it is unencrypted in transit; it carries public aggregates and no credentials.
  • Honesty notes: frequency and unit are NA — a census table is not a recurring series and the source states no units. Running indicators (CPI, GDP) are still not available as data: the CPI Explorer’s backend could not be identified (audit F-21), so monthly releases remain available as documents via knbs_publications(). The API answers unknown ids with HTTP 200 and the body errore; the package reports not-found.

Publications (Phase 4 completed)

The host that blocked Phase 4 recovered, its TLS chain fixed. The audit found the WordPress core REST API open over the site’s media library — roughly 1,600 documents with direct, ungated file URLs — while the Download Monitor catalogue remains gated and untouched.

  • knbs_publications() searches statistical releases, reports and workbooks, with free-text, format and reference-year filters.
  • knbs_download_publication() downloads one publication through the verifying download layer: official filename preserved, a web page arriving in place of a document refused, SHA-256 recorded, provenance sidecar written.
  • Honesty notes, both from the audit: release_date is the site’s upload date, not the publication’s reference period — the year column is read from the title and is NA when the title names none. And the media library also holds speeches and forms; narrowing to what you mean is the caller’s query.
  • The format filter is applied client-side even when the source also filtered, after the survey audit showed this family of APIs can silently ignore query parameters.

knbsdata 0.1.0

First release. It covers survey and census study discovery through the Kenya National Data Archive, and nothing else — see vignette("source-status") for what that excludes and why.

Survey catalogue

  • knbs_search_surveys() searches the study catalogue, with filters for free text, reference year, producer and access type.
  • knbs_survey_metadata() retrieves a study’s full descriptive record. An identifier it does not recognise falls back to searching the catalogue: one match is used, several are reported so you can choose, none is a plain not-found.
  • knbs_variables() searches variable metadata without downloading microdata, optionally retrieving each variable’s full record.
  • knbs_survey_files() lists a study’s data files with their access conditions.
  • knbs_download_microdata() refuses, explains that the archive requires an account, and points at the official access process. It exists so the refusal is explicit rather than looking like an oversight.

Provenance

  • knbs_metadata() returns the provenance record attached to every object: the source, the retrieval time, the release date, the access conditions and the package version.
  • knbs_cite() builds a citation in plain, BibTeX or RIS form. Where the archive states a required citation, that text wins and the package adds only the retrieval information.
  • Provenance survives row subsetting.

Sources and health

  • knbs_sources() reports what the package knows about each source and how far it has been verified.
  • knbs_status() reports source health. Offline by default in any non-interactive session, so checks and CI never depend on a live service. Sources with unverified endpoints are never contacted, even when a live check is requested.

Configuration and caching

  • knbs_options() and knbs_option(), backed by ordinary R options under the knbsdata. prefix.
  • knbs_cache_dir(), knbs_cache_info(), knbs_cache_clear() and knbs_cache_prune(). Entries are keyed on the source, operation, normalised query and parser version, checksummed, and written atomically. An entry that fails its checksum is discarded and refetched rather than returned.

Behaviour worth knowing

  • Every failure carries a knbs_error_* class. Nothing returns partial data dressed up as a result.
  • A login gate signalled by an HTTP Refresh header — which is how the archive gates downloads — is raised as knbs_error_authentication_required, not mistaken for an empty but successful response.
  • Responses are checked for the fields their operation requires, because the archive answers unknown paths with 200 and a study record rather than a 404. A payload arriving from the wrong place raises knbs_error_schema_changed.
  • Access types are translated into a canonical vocabulary. public_use means public-use files exist; it does not mean they can be downloaded.
  • No test touches the network.

Known limitations

  • Publications, aggregate indicators and geographic reference data are not implemented. All three live on a host that was unavailable throughout the source audit and every re-check, so its endpoints were never verified and no adapter was written.
  • Microdata cannot be downloaded, by design.
  • Documentation files are not listed: the archive publishes no machine-readable listing of questionnaires, reports or technical documents.
  • Variable documentation is missing for some studies, which returns zero rows.

Internal

  • A download layer — streaming, type verification, SHA-256, provenance sidecars, manifests and archive path-traversal protection — is built and tested but not yet reachable, since no supported source permits a download.
